newFindings.title: The second assent re-check may resolve against the frozen snapshot rather than the live root
newFindings.selector: assemble-records.successor.v1.py:480 vs :124, with source_path at :59-60 and accepted_files assigned at :52 and :127
newFindings.detail: ref() resolves through source_path(), which returns snapshotRoot/rel once rel is in accepted_files and root/rel otherwise. accepted_files is empty at the primary check (:124, so it reads the live root, matching what bind verified) but populated by the re-check (:480). If the assent path is itself inside the accepted design subject, :480 compares immutable snapshot bytes and would not detect a live-root mutation during assembly. Practical impact is minimal: the assent CONTENT is read once at :125 before any output, and the recorded digest at :571 is the verified assent_ref, so nothing emitted depends on the :480 read. The primary pre-output guard is unaffected.
newFindings.reproducer: scratch/v06_f5.py c_recheckResolution (static line/ordering analysis; the real candidate-subject manifest is not among the inputs, so whether the assent is pinned inside it could not be determined here).
newFindings.minimalRemedy: Re-check against the live root explicitly, e.g. assert digest(root / assent_ref['path']) == assent_ref['sha256'], so the guard is independent of accepted_files population order.

newFindings.title: freeze-application.py still re-asserts only the finalizer selftest, not the new current-tool receipts
newFindings.detail: The F8 correction produces a hash-bound receipt of the freshly executed envelope and retain suites, and prepare-validation itself asserts exit 0 and empty failure lists at :104-105, so the gate exists at production time. freeze still asserts only selftest['sourceSha256'] == sha(staged finalizer) and does not re-assert the new receipt. Because the stage cannot exist unless prepare-validation succeeded, this is a defence-in-depth gap rather than an open hole.
newFindings.reproducer: scratch/v01_diff.py (freeze-application.py is unchanged between v1 and v2) plus the read of prepare-validation.py:86-109.
newFindings.minimalRemedy: Add an assertion in freeze mirroring the finalizer one, e.g. load support/current-application-tool-checks.v1.json and assert every run exitCode==0 and every sourceFiles row matches the staged copy.

newFindings.title: check-retain-public.v1.py has no --report guard and writes fixed names into its own directory

limitations: This is a tooling re-review. It is not an application ACCEPT, not design acceptance, and awards no grade.

No application, receipt binding, freeze, launch, retention, or activation was performed against any real subject. All fixtures were synthetic and disposable; every write stayed under this runtime's scratch/ and per-case temporary directories.

The full application-successor root is still unavailable, so assemble-records.successor.v1.py, prepare-validation.py, freeze-application.py, verify-applied.py and the two reference-suite runners were NOT executed end to end. F5 was verified by executing the assembler PROLOGUE truncated at line 131 (before out.mkdir at 152) combined with an AST line-order proof, not by a full assembly. F8 was verified by extracting and running the bounded lines 86-109 block verbatim-equivalent in a disposable directory, not by running prepare-validation.py end to end. Both bounded scopes are stated rather than presented as full runs.
G2 could not be resolved either way because the real candidate-subject manifest is not among the inputs, so whether the Codex assent path is pinned inside the accepted design subject is unknown here.

check-retain-public.v1.py was read at its head and by targeted search, then executed in full; its 69 assertions were exercised rather than line-by-line reviewed. The four historical counterexample-fixture files were hashed and executed as the suite's contrast case, not line-reviewed.

The Grok vendor path was again exercised only at library level. No Grok or Claude CLI was run, no ~/.grok or ~/.claude session directory was read, and no real private CLI content of any kind was accessed. Every sanitizer sentinel was an invented synthetic string.
G1's practical reach depends on what a real Claude application reviewer chooses to name its authored files; the launch prompt directs it to review.md and review.json, which are unaffected.
In-process module probes ran under host python3 3.14.6 with -B; subprocess suites ran under the reference interpreter 3.12.13 -I -B. The two were not exhaustively cross-run.
All 32 product qualification gates remain unperformed and condition 5 remains NOT MET. Design acceptance is a separate question this review does not reach.
